newsitem.title: INDIA: India's oil imports to rise to $9.0 bln in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India's oil imports to rise to $9.0 bln in 96/97.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said the nation's oil import bill in 1996/97 (April-March) is likely to go up to $9.0 billion against an earlier estimate of $7.6 billion, Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Monday.
"The oil import bill is likely to increase to 9.0 billion dollars as against the provision of 7.6 billion dollars," PTI quoted Chidambaram as saying in the upper house of parliament.
India imports about 40 percent of its oil and product needs. This cost around $6.5 billion in 1995/96 and accounts for just over 20 percent of the country's total import bill.
Chidambaram said the oil output for the current fiscal year would be lower than projections made three months ago. The finance minister did not give the output projections.
Chidambaram justified the recent increase in domestic oil prices saying the oil import bill would have been worse if prices had not been hiked.

"Much against our expectations of flow of oil from Iraq, we apprehend there might not be any oil outflow from the gulf region for the present, aggravating the oil situation," the finance minister said.
